title: Write modes and read bounds
prompt: This program writes the 5 lesson invoices, 2 of them paid, to a database table several times and reads it back. Their totals are 244, 232, 469.50, 283.50 and 245. What does it print? Type each line on its own line.
program:
url = "jdbc:sqlite:/tmp/sales.db"
invoices.coalesce(1).write.jdbc(url, "invoices", mode="overwrite")
invoices.coalesce(1).write.jdbc(url, "invoices", mode="append")
print(spark.read.jdbc(url, "invoices").count())

invoices.coalesce(1).write.jdbc(url, "invoices", mode="ignore")
paid = spark.read.jdbc(url, "(SELECT invoice_id FROM invoices WHERE status = 'paid') AS paid")
print(paid.count())

invoices.coalesce(1).write.jdbc(url, "invoices", mode="overwrite")
parts = spark.read.jdbc(url, "invoices", column="total_amount", lowerBound=240, upperBound=250, numPartitions=2)
print(parts.count())
hints: `append` adds the rows again without checking for repeats.
`ignore` does nothing when the table already exists, and the subquery runs on whatever the table holds.
The bounds of a partitioned read only decide where the slices are cut. Do they remove any rows?
